basic_information.name: Voyage AI (now part of MongoDB)
basic_information.creator: Voyage AI, founded by Tengyu Ma, Hong Liu, and Kaidi Cao (Stanford researchers). Acquired by MongoDB in February 2025 for $220 million. Now operates as 'Voyage AI by MongoDB'.
basic_information.description: Voyage AI provides state-of-the-art embedding and reranking models purpose-built for retrieval and RAG applications. The company differentiates through domain-specialized models (code, finance, legal, multilingual) that consistently outperform competitors across 100+ retrieval benchmarks. Its latest Voyage 4 series (January 2026) introduces a shared embedding space enabling cross-model compatibility, and its multimodal models handle interleaved text, images, and video without complex document parsing. Voyage AI was notably the embedding provider recommended by Anthropic before its acquisition by MongoDB. The company was founded in September 2023, raised $28M in Series A funding (October 2024), and was acquired by MongoDB for $220M just 17 months after launch — one of the fastest startup-to-acquisition cycles in the AI infrastructure space.
basic_information.release_date: Founded September 2023. Voyage-3 released September 2024. Voyage-3-large released January 2025. Voyage-3.5 released May 2025. Rerank-2.5 released August 2025. Voyage-context-3 released July 2025. Voyage 4 series and voyage-multimodal-3.5 released January 15, 2026.
basic_information.license: Proprietary (API-only access for most models). voyage-4-nano is the first open-weights model, available on Hugging Face.
basic_information.github_stars: voyageai-python SDK: ~88 GitHub stars (as of early 2026). Modest open-source footprint because the core models are proprietary API-served. Additional repos: voyageai-aws (deployment notebooks), voyageai-typescript.

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Cloud API (serverless). Models are accessed via REST API endpoints hosted by Voyage AI / MongoDB. Also available as AWS Marketplace SageMaker model packages (deployable into customer VPC as real-time endpoints or batch transform jobs), Azure Marketplace deployment (data stays in customer virtual network), and GCP deployment via MongoDB Atlas. Batch API available with 33% cost discount and 12-hour completion window.
technical_architecture.language: Model implementation undisclosed (transformer-based neural network architecture). Client SDKs available in Python (voyageai) and TypeScript/JavaScript (voyageai npm). API follows REST interface with JSON request/response format.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Voyage 4 series: voyage-4-large supports 2048 (default), 1024, 512, 256 dimensions. voyage-3.5 / voyage-3.5-lite: 2048, 1024 (default), 512, 256 dimensions via Matryoshka learning. voyage-3-large: 1024 dimensions (default). voyage-code-3: 2048, 1024 (default), 512, 256. voyage-context-3: 1024 (default), 256, 512, 2048. All recent models support Matryoshka dimensionality reduction and multiple quantization options (float32, int8, uint8, binary).
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: N/A — Voyage AI is an embedding and reranking generation service, not a vector database. It produces dense vector embeddings compatible with any indexing algorithm (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, flat, etc.) in any vector store. Binary quantization output (512-dim binary) enables 192x cheaper storage while matching float-based models of higher dimensions.
technical_architecture.scalability: Serverless API with automatic scaling. Context window: 32,000 tokens for most models (voyage-3.5, voyage-3-large, voyage-code-3, voyage-context-3, rerank-2.5). Reranker query limit: 8,000 tokens. AWS SageMaker deployment supports real-time inference endpoints and batch transform jobs for bulk processing. MongoDB Atlas integration provides managed scaling.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: 1) Voyage AI hosted API (api.voyageai.com / MongoDB-managed). 2) AWS Marketplace: SageMaker model packages deployable into customer VPC (real-time endpoints or batch transform). 3) Azure Marketplace: models run within customer virtual network, data never leaves VNet. 4) MongoDB Atlas: embedded within MongoDB's cloud platform. 5) GCP: newly available as of January 2026. voyage-4-nano available on Hugging Face for local/on-device deployment.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector retrieval via high-quality embeddings. Dedicated reranking models (rerank-2.5, rerank-2.5-lite) for second-stage retrieval refinement with instruction-following capabilities. No native sparse retrieval (BM25/SPLADE), but embeddings integrate seamlessly with hybrid search implementations in vector databases. Contextualized chunk embeddings (voyage-context-3) encode both chunk content and source document context in a single vector, eliminating need for metadata augmentation.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Voyage-context-3 introduces contextualized chunk embeddings that automatically capture both chunk-level detail and global document context without manual metadata or context augmentation. This is a significant innovation — the model sees all chunks simultaneously and intelligently injects relevant global information into individual chunk embeddings. Compatible with all standard chunking approaches (fixed-size, semantic, recursive). The 32,000-token context window accommodates large documents. Outperforms Jina-v3 late chunking by 23.66% and Anthropic's contextual retrieval by 20.54% on chunk-level retrieval tasks.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in reranking via rerank-2.5 and rerank-2.5-lite models. Key features: (1) Instruction-following capability — users can steer relevance scoring with natural language instructions; (2) 32K token context length (8x Cohere Rerank v3.5); (3) Outperforms Cohere Rerank v3.5 by 7.94% on 93 retrieval datasets; (4) On the MAIR instruction-following benchmark, outperforms Cohere by 12.70%. Pricing: same per-token model as embeddings, first 200M tokens free.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: voyage-multimodal-3 embeds interleaved text and images (screenshots of PDFs, tables, figures, slides) capturing textual and visual features (font size, layout, whitespace) without complex document parsing. Outperforms OpenAI CLIP large and Cohere multimodal v3 by 41-43% on table/figure retrieval. voyage-multimodal-3.5 (January 2026) adds video frame support, is the first production-grade multimodal embedding model with Matryoshka dimensionality, and supports interleaved text, images, and video in a single embedding.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No native graph RAG capabilities. Voyage AI is an embedding and reranking provider. Knowledge graph construction and graph-enhanced retrieval must be implemented externally. However, Voyage embeddings can be used as the vector component in hybrid graph+vector RAG architectures.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: No built-in citation or grounding verification in the embedding/reranking models themselves. However, the high retrieval accuracy (especially with reranking) helps ensure the correct source documents are retrieved, which indirectly supports citation grounding at the application layer. MongoDB Atlas integration may provide document-level tracking for source attribution.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: 32,000-token context window across most models — among the largest in the embedding model space (8x larger than OpenAI's 8,192 tokens). voyage-context-3's contextualized chunk embeddings capture document-level context within chunk embeddings, reducing information loss from chunking. Matryoshka dimensionality reduction (256, 512, 1024, 2048) and quantization (float32, int8, uint8, binary) allow trading off precision for storage efficiency. Binary 512-dim embeddings match OpenAI float 3072-dim in accuracy at 192x less storage cost.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: API-based latency varies by model size and network conditions. Voyage-3.5-lite and voyage-4-lite optimized for lower latency. The Voyage 4 shared embedding space allows using voyage-4-lite for high-throughput queries while maintaining compatibility with voyage-4-large indexed documents. AWS SageMaker real-time endpoints provide dedicated inference capacity. Specific p50/p99 latency numbers not publicly disclosed. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Batch API available with 12-hour completion window and 33% cost discount for bulk processing. AWS SageMaker deployment supports batch transform jobs for high-volume offline embedding. The Voyage 4 series' cross-model compatibility enables throughput optimization: index with voyage-4-large, query with faster voyage-4-lite or voyage-4-nano. Rate limits not publicly disclosed for the API tier. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Voyage-4-large: top of RTEB leaderboard (January 2026), superseding voyage-3-large. Voyage-3.5: 64.6% MTEB, outperforms OpenAI-v3-large by 8.26% average across domains. Voyage-3-large: outperforms OpenAI-v3-large by 9.74% and Cohere-v3-English by 20.71% across 100 datasets in 8 domains. Voyage-context-3: outperforms OpenAI-v3-large by 14.24% and Cohere-v4 by 12.56% on chunk-level retrieval. Rerank-2.5: outperforms Cohere Rerank v3.5 by 7.94% on standard retrieval. All metrics measured via NDCG@10.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: Evaluated across 100 datasets spanning 8 domains: technical documentation, code, law, finance, web reviews, multilingual, long documents, and conversations. Voyage-4-large is #1 on the RTEB (Retrieval Text Embedding Benchmark) leaderboard as of January 2026. Domain-specific performance: voyage-law-2-harvey (custom legal model trained on 20B+ legal tokens) reportedly achieved 25% reduction in irrelevant search results for Harvey. Multimodal: voyage-multimodal-3 outperforms OpenAI CLIP large by 41.44% on table/figure retrieval and 26.54% on document screenshot retrieval.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Comprehensive framework support: LangChain (VoyageAIEmbeddings, VoyageAIRerank Document Compressor), LlamaIndex (VoyageEmbedding, VoyageAI Rerank Node Postprocessor), Haystack (Voyage AI Embedder, Voyage AI Reranker), liteLLM (Voyage provider). Vector database integrations: Pinecone, Milvus, Qdrant, Weaviate, Chroma, MongoDB Atlas Vector Search (native post-acquisition), DataStax Astra DB. Also compatible with Vercel AI SDK via community provider.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Voyage embeddings produce standard dense vectors compatible with any LLM for RAG generation. Historically recommended by Anthropic as their preferred embedding provider (referenced in Claude documentation and cookbooks). Compatible with OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, open-source models, and any LLM. Post-acquisition, natively integrated with MongoDB Atlas Vector Search for seamless retrieval+storage.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: No dedicated Voyage AI MCP server identified as of February 2026. However, Voyage AI integrations exist within LangChain and LlamaIndex, both of which have MCP adapters, enabling indirect MCP connectivity. MongoDB Atlas may develop MCP integration as part of its broader AI platform.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: N/A — Voyage AI is a pure embedding and reranking generation API. Data source connectivity handled by orchestration frameworks. Post-acquisition MongoDB Atlas integration means documents stored in MongoDB can be embedded and searched natively without external pipeline tools. AWS SageMaker deployment integrates with S3 and other AWS data sources.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: No dedicated observability platform from Voyage AI. Compatible with LangSmith, Langfuse, and Arize Phoenix via their LangChain/LlamaIndex instrumentation integrations. MongoDB Atlas provides built-in monitoring for vector search operations. API usage tracking available via Voyage AI dashboard and billing management. [uncertain]

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Usage-based pay-per-token pricing. Charges based on number of tokens in documents and queries. Batch API offers 33% discount with 12-hour completion window. AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace pricing varies by instance type for self-hosted deployment.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: First 200 million tokens free for each account (applies to both embedding models and reranking models separately). This is generous — sufficient to embed roughly 400,000 pages of text or process significant reranking workloads for prototyping and early production.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Current pricing (as of 2026): voyage-3.5: $0.06/1M tokens. voyage-3.5-lite: $0.02/1M tokens. voyage-context-3: $0.18/1M tokens. voyage-multimodal-3: $0.06/1M tokens. Rerank-2.5: not separately disclosed but follows per-token model. Batch API: 33% discount on all models. Example: Embedding 1M documents (~500 tokens each = 500M tokens) with voyage-3.5 costs $30 (standard) or ~$20 (batch). With voyage-3.5-lite: $10 standard. OpenAI text-embedding-3-large comparison: $0.13/1M tokens — Voyage-3.5 is 2.2x cheaper with better benchmark scores. Voyage 4 series pricing not yet publicly confirmed. [uncertain]
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Embedding costs are modest relative to overall RAG infrastructure. For 1M documents with voyage-3.5-lite: ~$10 one-time embedding + negligible query costs. Major TCO components: vector database hosting ($20-500+/month), LLM generation costs (typically 10-100x embedding costs), and engineering time. Post-MongoDB acquisition, using MongoDB Atlas for both document storage and vector search may simplify TCO by eliminating a separate vector DB. Self-hosted via AWS SageMaker adds compute costs but provides data sovereignty. Matryoshka dimensionality reduction (e.g., 256 instead of 1024) and binary quantization can reduce vector storage costs by 8-192x.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in specialized embedding models for domain-specific retrieval. Consistently #1 on retrieval benchmarks (RTEB, internal 100-dataset evaluation). The MongoDB acquisition positioned Voyage AI as part of a major database platform, giving it enterprise distribution advantages. Unique position as the only major embedding provider with both domain-specific and multimodal models, plus built-in reranking.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Harvey (legal AI — co-developed voyage-law-2-harvey custom model trained on 20B+ legal tokens), Replit (code search and retrieval), Anthropic (recommended embedding partner, referenced in Claude documentation), LangChain (ecosystem integration partner), Vanta (security compliance), SK Telecom (telecommunications). Post-acquisition: all MongoDB Atlas customers gain native access.
adoption_and_market.community_size: voyageai-python GitHub: ~88 stars (small, reflecting proprietary API model). Blog and documentation are well-maintained with detailed benchmark reports. Community primarily accessed through MongoDB's broader ecosystem post-acquisition. Active presence on X/Twitter (@VoyageAI). Integration presence across LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, and major vector databases suggests broad developer adoption despite small open-source footprint.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Series A: $28M (October 2024), led by CRV with participation from Wing Venture Capital, Conviction, Snowflake, Databricks, Pear VC, Tectonic Capital, Mayfield, and Fusion Fund. Acquired by MongoDB for $220M (announced February 24, 2025) — a 7.9x return on invested capital in approximately 5 months post-Series A. Total company lifespan from founding to acquisition: 17 months. MongoDB (acquirer): NYSE-listed, ~$20B+ market cap.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: OpenAI text-embedding-3 (market leader by adoption, $0.13/1M tokens for large), Cohere embed-v4 (strong multilingual, 100+ languages, enterprise-focused), Jina Embeddings v4 (multimodal, open-source-friendly), Google Gemini Embedding (Vertex AI ecosystem). Open-source alternatives: BGE (BAAI), E5 (Microsoft), GTE (Alibaba), Nomic Embed. Key Voyage differentiators: (1) domain-specific models (code, law, finance) with custom training capability, (2) contextualized chunk embeddings (voyage-context-3), (3) multimodal with video support, (4) built-in reranking, (5) MongoDB integration for unified storage+retrieval, (6) open-weights voyage-4-nano for local development.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Ideal for startups building RAG systems in specialized domains — especially legal tech, fintech, code intelligence, and multilingual applications where domain-specific embedding quality directly impacts product quality. Best for teams that: (1) need top-tier retrieval accuracy without training their own models, (2) work in vertical domains where generic embeddings underperform, (3) want reranking built into the same provider as embeddings. Budget: very accessible — 200M free tokens covers extensive prototyping, and $0.02-0.06/1M tokens for production is competitive. Team size: any (API-based, no ML infrastructure needed). The MongoDB acquisition makes Voyage especially attractive for startups already using MongoDB — zero additional vendor management. Consider alternatives when: open-source self-hosting is required (use Jina or BGE), total cost must be zero (use open-source models), or you need maximum ecosystem flexibility without database lock-in.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Voyage AI API (buy) when: domain-specific retrieval quality matters, team lacks ML expertise for model training/hosting, data volume is moderate (up to hundreds of millions of documents), and the 200M free tier covers your prototyping phase. Use voyage-4-nano (hybrid) when: you need local development/testing without API costs, want to evaluate before committing to API. Consider self-hosted open-source when: data cannot leave your infrastructure, embedding costs exceed $500/month making self-hosting economical, or you need fine-tuning control beyond what Voyage offers. MongoDB Atlas + Voyage AI is the path of least resistance for startups already on MongoDB — eliminates the separate vector database entirely. AWS SageMaker deployment provides middle ground: Voyage models in your VPC with data sovereignty.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 30 minutes (pip install voyageai + API key + 5 lines of Python). MVP with full RAG pipeline using LangChain/LlamaIndex: 1-2 days. Production deployment with Voyage embeddings + reranking: 1-2 weeks. MongoDB Atlas native integration: fastest path for MongoDB users (minutes to enable). AWS SageMaker deployment: 1-2 weeks for VPC-isolated setup. The 200M free token tier means zero cost during development.
key_lessons: 1. Leverage domain-specific models for vertical products — if building legal tech, fintech, or developer tools, Voyage's specialized models (voyage-law-2, voyage-finance-2, voyage-code-3) provide measurable retrieval quality improvements over general-purpose embeddings. Harvey's 25% reduction in irrelevant results with custom legal embeddings demonstrates the business impact.

2. Use voyage-context-3 to solve the chunking problem — rather than spending engineering time on elaborate chunking strategies, metadata augmentation, or contextual retrieval hacks, voyage-context-3 automatically captures document-level context in chunk embeddings. It outperforms both late chunking and Anthropic's contextual retrieval approach.

3. Adopt a two-stage retrieval pipeline (embed + rerank) — Voyage's rerank-2.5 with instruction-following can add 8-12% accuracy improvement on top of initial retrieval. The instruction-following feature lets you dynamically adjust relevance criteria without re-embedding.

4. Use Matryoshka dimensions and quantization to manage costs — binary 512-dimension embeddings from Voyage match OpenAI float 3072-dimension in accuracy at 192x less storage. Start with full dimensions for quality validation, then compress for production to cut vector DB costs.

5. The Voyage AI acquisition story is a lesson in AI startup strategy — $220M exit in 17 months by focusing on a critical infrastructure layer (embeddings), building measurably superior domain-specific models, and establishing partnerships with key ecosystem players (Anthropic, MongoDB). For entrepreneurs: embedding quality is a defensible moat when paired with domain expertise.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: No dedicated no-code interface for embedding generation. However, MongoDB Atlas provides a visual interface for configuring vector search indexes with Voyage AI embeddings. Third-party no-code platforms (Flowise, Dify, AnythingLLM, Relevance AI) support Voyage AI through their LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations.

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from Voyage AI's official blog posts and documentation, MongoDB investor relations announcements, TechCrunch reporting, PR Newswire press releases, Inc. Magazine, VentureBeat, InfoWorld, AWS Marketplace listings, and multiple independent benchmark comparisons.
confidence.cross_reference: MongoDB acquisition price ($220M) confirmed across Bloomberg, Inc. Magazine, PR Newswire, and MongoDB investor relations. Series A funding ($28M, CRV-led) confirmed by TechCrunch and Tracxn. Benchmark performance (outperforming OpenAI by 8-14% depending on model) confirmed across Voyage AI blog, MongoDB blog, Agentset leaderboard, and multiple independent comparisons. Pricing ($0.06/1M tokens for voyage-3.5) confirmed on Voyage AI docs and MongoDB billing pages. Harvey partnership confirmed by Harvey's blog and MongoDB press releases.
confidence.caveats: Benchmark results are primarily self-reported by Voyage AI on their own evaluation suite of 100 datasets — while the methodology appears rigorous (NDCG@10, standardized datasets), independent third-party verification on all claims is limited. Post-MongoDB acquisition, product direction may shift toward MongoDB ecosystem lock-in. Voyage 4 series pricing not yet publicly confirmed as of February 2026. The 'recommended by Anthropic' relationship may evolve now that Voyage is owned by MongoDB (a competitor in the AI data layer). Rapidly evolving space — performance advantages may narrow as OpenAI, Cohere, and Jina release newer models.
confidence.security_posture: AWS VPC deployment ensures data never leaves customer infrastructure. Azure deployment keeps data within customer virtual network with Azure as sole sub-processor. Standard API: data retained per privacy policy with opt-out for training usage. No publicly disclosed SOC 2 or GDPR certification for Voyage AI's own infrastructure, though AWS and Azure deployments inherit their compliance certifications. MongoDB Atlas adds enterprise security features (encryption at rest, audit logging, RBAC). General embedding risk: embedding vectors can theoretically be inverted to approximate original text (embedding inversion attacks) — this is a general industry risk, not Voyage-specific.
